sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Ansar Allah Health Ministry via AP, Nov 7] Airstrikes hit homes in the village of al-Shariya, Bani Hushaysh district, Sanaa province, on Saturday afternoon, killing at least 22 people and wounding 30 others, mostly women and children. Ansar Allah Health Ministry spokesman Anees Alasbahi accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out the strikes; Saudi Arabia has not commented. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Saba/Al-Masirah via AFP/Dawn, Nov 7] 'The number of victims of the Saudi enemy warplane massacre in the Al-Shariya area... has risen to 22 citizens, most of them children and women, while the number of wounded has risen to 30.' Saba adds operations to recover victims from rubble were ongoing and 'aircraft targeted paramedics with two strikes.' [CONTEXT] The Times of Israel liveblog's earlier '10 killed in Bani Hashish' and '11 killed in Sanaa' entries are the SAME event at earlier tolls, not separate strikes. The Friday Taiz al-Hadara market toll of 30 killed / 8 wounded is already recorded (0100-02); the two-day toll across the two strikes is at least 52. Yemeni government forces claim 3 air attacks on Ansar Allah positions in al-Misrakh, Taiz (AJ liveblog, in-window) -- see triage 1700-07(a).
sections.what_verified: AP (T1) carries the ministry spokesman's account on the record; AFP (T1, via Dawn) carries the Saba/Al-Masirah toll; Press TV (T3 STATE IR) carries the same toll. Saba/Al-Masirah are untiered (not in registry) -- attribution only.
sections.what_disputed: Saudi Arabia has not commented; AP could not independently verify the claims or the attribution to Saudi Arabia. The mirror dispute continues: for the Friday Taiz market attack, Yemeni government forces blame the Ansar Allah and say no military aircraft operated in the area (recorded 0100-02). No independent casualty verification exists for al-Shariya.
sections.why_matters: 22 dead in one village -- mostly women and children. Saudi Arabia won't say a word. The Yemen war is back, and the toll in two days is 52.

totw_analysis: Our read: 22 dead in one village -- mostly women and children. Saudi Arabia won't say a word. The Yemen war is back, and the toll in two days is 52. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Saudi bombs on civilian homes -- or Ansar Allah human shields? Who is responsible for Yemen's dead children?
